AUGUSTA, MAINE – Secretary of State Shenna Bellows today traveled to Brunswick Town Hall to mark the start of in-person, no-excuse absentee voting in Maine today. 

“Maine is always a national leader in voter turnout, and we saw record turnout in the June primary. In person absentee voting – Maine’s version of early voting – is part of the special sauce that makes voting convenient to the citizenry and drives up turnout,” said Secretary Bellows. “Anyone can vote early for any reason starting today until October 29, and there are lots of ways to vote absentee – in person, by mail or utilizing a secure ballot drop box.”

This week, voters who are not able to make it to the polls on Election Day or who simply wish to avoid the crowds can begin casting absentee ballots, either in-person at their local town hall or by mailing back their signed and sealed ballot or dropping it in a local secure ballot box. As of Friday, October 2, more than 70,000 Mainers had requested an absentee ballot. Absentee ballot reports are posted on Tuesdays and Thursdays on the Secretary of State’s website.  

Brunswick Town Clerk Fran Smith joined Secretary Bellows to talk about the tasks and challenges that face local election officials this election cycle and why Mainers can expect business as usual for the November 3 General Election.

“This is a busy but exciting time for our office, as I know it is for towns across the state,” said Brunswick Town Clerk Fran Smith. “Our local staff, as well as volunteers on Election Day, are so incredibly vital to ensuring everything runs smoothly right up through the counting of the ballots after the polls close on Election Day.”

As absentee voting gets underway, Secretary Bellows urged voters to make a plan to ensure their ballots are returned by close of polls on Election Day. In Maine, only those ballots received by close of polls are counted, regardless of postmark. Maine offers an online absentee ballot tracking service for voters to track the status of their absentee ballot to be sure that the clerk has received and accepted the ballot. If a voter’s ballot has not been received by Election Day, voters may go in person to the polls on November 3 to request that the missing absentee ballot be rejected or cancelled and cast a vote in person.

“The election should be business as usual this year because the election laws haven’t changed, but sometimes life gets in the way. We have all unfortunately experienced frustration with the postal service and things from everyday mail to prescriptions not arriving in a timely manner,” Secretary Bellows said. “That’s why it can be so helpful to vote early.”

“It’s exciting – Election Day will be here before we know it, and now is the time to make your voting plan,” she said.

Temporary Changes to Referral and Authorization Processes Ending November 30, 2026

Oct 06, 2026

Beginning December 1, 2026, the Department will require members to complete a Single Assessment within the past 12 months before processing referrals, prior authorization requests, and continued stay reviews for children’s medium- and high-intensity services. 

As previously communicated, the Department temporarily reinstated direct-to-provider referral and prior authorization processes while operational challenges with the Single Assessment process were being addressed. That temporary process will end November 30, 2026. 

The Single Assessment process has stabilized significantly, with assessments now completed in an average of 7.5 business days after a request is submitted. 

Thank you for your continued partnership with the Single Assessment process.

New MaineCare Partner Portal: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Requirements

Oct 06, 2026

As a reminder, the new MaineCare Partner Portal is scheduled to go live on October 12, 2026, at 8:00 AM. The new portal will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal and will require Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). Read below for more information and steps you will need to take to sign into the MaineCare Partner Portal starting on October 12. 

For all information about the upcoming changes to MIHMS, see the “HealthPAS Online Portal” section of the Provider Resources page.  

Multi-Factor Authenticator (MFA) 

MFA adds a second verification step after entering your password. This is an important new security measure to protect the sensitive information held in the Portal. You will have three options to choose from for your additional authentication factor; you must choose one.

Follow the instructions below for first-time setup of the option you choose. 

  1. Microsoft Authenticator 

The Microsoft Authenticator app is the recommended MFA method because it offers the highest level of protection over other methods. Download the Microsoft Authenticator app now on a smartphone or tablet so that you are ready to use it on October 12. 

No sooner than October 12, follow these steps to set up MFA via the app:  

Trading Partners with existing (migrated) Portal accounts: 

  • Open the Microsoft Authenticator app. 
  • Click “Sign In” on the MaineCare Partner Portal; you will see a User Details window pop up. 
  • Click the QR code scanner in the Microsoft Authenticator app and scan the QR code displayed on the Portal’s User Details window.  

Trading Partners without existing (new or non-migrated) Portal accounts will set this up as part of the registration process.

 

  1. Text/Call 

Text (SMS) or call verification is available as an MFA option through September 2027.  

No sooner than October 12, follow these steps to set up MFA via text (SMS) or call: 

Trading Partners with existing (migrated) Portal accounts: 

  • Click “Sign In” on the MaineCare Partner Portal; you will see a User Details window pop up. 
  • Select the “Text/call” option then click “Continue.” 
  • Enter a phone number, request a code or call, then verify the code. The phone number you provide during setup will be saved as your registered MFA contact method and will be used for future authentication and account verification activities. 

Trading Partners without existing (new or non-migrated) Portal accounts will set this up as part of the registration process.

 

  1. Email 

Email verification is available as an MFA option through September 2027. 

No sooner than October 12, follow these steps to set up MFA via email: 

Trading Partners with existing (migrated) Portal accounts: 

  • Click “Sign In” on the MaineCare Partner Portal; you will see a User Details window pop up. 
  • Select the “Email” option then click “Continue.” 
  • Enter an email address, request a code, then verify the code. The email address you provide during setup will be saved as your registered MFA contact method and will be used for future authentication and account verification activities. 

Trading Partners without existing (new or non-migrated) Portal accounts will set this up as part of the registration process. 

 

For additional instructions on both initial setup and ongoing use of MFA, including screenshots, please reference the job aid MaineCare Partner Portal MFA Setup and Access Job Aid. 

  • You can find this job aid and other supporting resources through the MMIS Learning Center. Search for the course “ME – MIHMS Upgrade Documentation,” enroll in the course, then look for the job aid in the documentation list. 
  • Starting October 12, 2026, this job aid will also be available in the MaineCare Partner Portal under the Provider tab > Provider Manuals subtab. 

Need Help? 

If you have questions about these instructions, please call Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585. 

Thank you for preparing in advance for a smooth transition to the new MaineCare Partner Portal.

Maine Senate Confirms Vaughan Woodruff as Chair of the State Workforce Development Board

October 5, 2026

For Immediate Release

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - The Maine Senate confirmed Vaughan Woodruff, principal of EquinoxDG, to a second term as chair of the State Workforce Development Board (SWDB). Gov. Janet Mills announced her nomination of Woodruff on Sept. 8, 2026. Woodruff has served as chair of the SWDB since 2023.

Prior to founding EquinoxDG, Woodruff was vice president of regulatory reform at the Interstate Renewable Energy Council and vice president of workforce development and interconnection strategy at ReVision Energy, where he oversaw the company's long-term strategic vision for training and talent development and developed nationally recognized registered apprenticeships in clean energy.

"The State Workforce Development Board plays a critical role in coordinating Maine's workforce development efforts to support economic growth and address workforce challenges," said Maine Department of Labor Commissioner Laura Fortman. "Vaughan Woodruff is a well-respected business leader with deep workforce expertise. His continued leadership will help maintain momentum as we strengthen Maine's workforce and economy."

"I appreciate the trust that Gov. Mills and the Maine Senate have placed in me through my nomination and confirmation to continue serving the people of Maine in this role," said Woodruff. "I feel privileged to work with the outstanding staff and members of the Board to increase the accessibility of the workforce system to Maine workers and businesses and to proactively address the workforce challenges ahead of us."

Woodruff is a seventh-generation Maine native who was raised in Pittsfield. He earned a bachelor's degree in civil engineering from the University of Maine and a master's degree in education from Prescott College in Arizona. Woodruff was the founder and CEO of Insource Renewables, an employee-owned solar company that was recognized as a Best for the World for Workers company by B Lab prior to its acquisition by ReVision Energy in 2021.

During Woodruff's tenure as chair, the SWDB has:

  • Launched Work Source Maine, the state's online resource connecting job seekers, students, parents, educators, career counselors and employers with resources to explore, plan and achieve career and workforce goals;

  • Launched the Maine Workforce Pell program, which expands federal Pell Grant eligibility to approved short-term, career-focused training programs that deliver industry-recognized credentials and measurable employment results, preparing students for in-demand occupations; and

  • Secured $15M+ in funding to support industry partnerships in advanced manufacturing, forest bioproducts and defense, and expand career exploration, job supports, and upskilling investments including registered pre-apprenticeships

As chair, Woodruff will continue to work with the SWDB, state agencies, education and training providers, employers and other partners to strengthen Maine's workforce development system and help connect Maine people with career opportunities.

Woodruff serves on the Electrical Technologies Advisory Committee at Kennebec Valley Community College and previously served on the Western Mountains Committee of the Maine Community Foundation and the Pittsfield Planning Board. Woodruff lives in Pittsfield with his wife, Holly Zadra, and their two sons, Eamon and Goran.

This poster explaining how to mark the ranked-choice ballot (PDF) is posted in every voting booth on Election Day.

Fact Sheet:

This PDF provides the facts voters need to know about voting in a ranked-choice election.

What is the process for tabulating ranked-choice ballots? (PDF)

Ranked choice voting results tabulation glossary

This glossary explains the terms used in the ranked-choice voting results grid that is produced to explain the results of any ranked-choice race. See our Election Results page.

Round 1

This is the first round of ranked-choice voting tabulation, which begins to apply the RCV rules onto the ballots that were cast on Election Day. (Note: The unofficial Election Day tally can be considered as Round 0). For example, if a voter did not mark any candidate as their first choice, their ballot was counted as blank on election night. In Round 1, if the voter marked the ballot for their second choice candidate, their vote is bumped up and counted, per the RCV rules.) Rounds continue until only two candidates remain and the winner is determined as the candidate with more than 50% of the votes in that final round.

Exhausted ballot

There are no valid votes in any ranking on the voter’s ballot for any continuing candidate (a candidate who is still in the race and has not been defeated). Types of exhausted ballots:

  • Exhausted choices: For those ballots that are exhausted by exhausted choices, all of the voter’s candidate choices have been eliminated from the race. (Note: If they cast a vote for a candidate who has been eliminated, their vote remains with that candidate, just as it would in a plurality race if they had voted for the losing candidate.)
  • Undervote: The voter did not mark any candidates, or refrained from ranking, in that choice category (1st, 2nd, 3rd). Those whose ballots are exhausted by undervote either didn’t vote in this race at all, or they left BOTH their first and second choices blank (in which case, we do not look any further down their ballot, per the RCV rules).
  • Overvote: The voter chose more than one candidate for that ranking. For example, the voter marked BOTH Candidate A and Candidate B as their choice.

Continuing ballots

All ballots that include a valid vote for a continuing candidate, and therefore have not been exhausted.

Transfer

The votes that go to a continuing candidate when another candidate is eliminated. This is determined by reviewing each ballot initially cast for the eliminated candidate. The elections software looks further down each voter’s ballot to see if the voter ranked another candidate who is still in the race, and if so, it moves or “transfers” their vote to that candidate (For example: Your vote transfers to your second choice candidate if your first choice candidate is eliminated from the race).

Total=

Ballot Exhausted by Overvotes + Ballot Exhausted by Undervotes + Exhausted Ballot + Continuing Ballots.

Board of Occupational Safety and Health to Host Listening Sessions on Proposed Indoor Air Quality Compliance Directive

October 6, 2026

For Immediate Release

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA - The Board of Occupational Safety and Health (BOSH) and the Maine Department of Labor Bureau of Labor Standards (BLS) Workplace Safety and Health Division invite interested parties and the public to participate in listening sessions on a proposed voluntary compliance directive on indoor air quality.

BOSH regulates and enforces workplace safety and health rules that apply to public employers, including state and local governmental agencies, school districts and quasi-governmental agencies. BOSH is considering publishing a voluntary compliance directive to help public employers monitor and maintain healthy indoor air quality in public workplaces. The proposed compliance directive is based in part on the research and recommendations of the Indoor Air Quality Advisory Group in 2025.

BOSH and BLS will host the following listening sessions:

  • Oct. 13, 2026, at 1 p.m. at the SafetyWorks! Training Institute, 45 Commerce Dr., Augusta

  • Nov. 2, 2026, at 3 p.m. by Zoom with a focus on public school and education employers https://mainestate.zoom.us/j/82302635655?pwd=b1nVGHTd2yeypvjPXwaJlAkK2YhjkL.1

  • Nov. 9, 2026, at 10 a.m. by Zoom https://mainestate.zoom.us/j/89708408033?pwd=XNUa0qqLPRczBcznzCrbdDmoBkbadP.1

If you require an accommodation or need an interpreter to participate in a listening session, please contact Rebecca Guppy at rebecca.guppy@maine.gov before Oct. 9, 2026, so services can be scheduled.

item.description: The Department of Energy ("DOE" or "the Department") is withdrawing the test procedure for commercial warm air furnaces adopted under the Energy Policy and Conservation Act, specifically appendix B, "Uniform Test Method for Measurement of the Energy Efficiency of Commercial Warm Air Furnaces (Thermal Efficiency Two)." Upon reconsideration, DOE has determined that appendix B would have an uncertain increase in representativeness that does not outweigh the likely increase in burden. DOE has also determined that withdrawing the appendix B test procedure would be consistent with the proposed Process Rule, which states that for certain categories of equipment, including CWAFs, DOE will adopt the industry test procedure, as contemplated by EPCA, except in very limited circumstances. Commercial warm air furnaces will continue to be subject to the testing requirements of appendix A, "Uniform Test Method for Measurement of the Energy Efficiency of Commercial Warm Air Furnaces (Thermal Efficiency)."

item.title: US Department of Labor cites Pennsylvania excavation employer for failing to provide trench protection following fatal trench cave-in — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
item.description: CHAMBERSBURG, PA – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited an excavation contractor for willful and serious safety violations after a young worker was fatally injured in a trench collapse. The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration opened an investigation into Jonas David Wagoner – doing business as J.D. Wagoner Excavating – on April 2, 2026, and found workers were installing a storm sewer system 12 feet below ground level in a trench that was not adequately protected from soil collapse. When a portion of the trench's wall failed, the unrestrained soil engulfed one worker. The agency issued a willful violation for failure to protect workers from cave-ins and two repeat violations for failing to assign a competent person to conduct daily trench inspections and removing employees from hazardous conditions.In addition, the employer received three serious violations for failure to provide construction hazard prevention training to employees, establish a safe means for workers to exit the excavation site, keep materials at least two feet from the edge of an excavation site, and restrain side materials from becoming roll-in hazards. OSHA proposed $254,884 in penalties. The employer has 15 business days from receiving receipt of its citations and penalties to request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Please check the OSHA establishment search page periodically for any changes in the inspection or penalty status.Visit OSHA’s website to learn about keeping workers safe around trenching and excavations. Employers can also contact the agency for information about OSHA’s compliance assistance resources and for free help on complying with OSHA standards.

Mr. Weiss contends that the ALJ erred in determining that his petition was untimely under 39-A M.R.S.A. § 321(2), and in concluding that even if the petition had been timely, Mr. Weiss did not establish that Maine Soapstone Company committed fraud. We disagree with Mr. Weiss’s contentions and affirm the decision.

MaineCare in Education: Updated Joint Individual Education Program (IEP) Guidance for School Health-Related Services

Oct 08, 2026

As a reminder, all providers who deliver services following the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) must ensure all MaineCare-covered services are documented following the Department of Health and Human Services/Maine Department of Education Joint IEP Guidance document. 

The Maine Department of Education has released updated Joint IEP Guidance to help schools follow federal and state requirements. The updated guidance was developed through a collaborative effort and is available on the MaineCare in Education web page. 

DOE first released the Joint Guidance on August 28, 2026, and has re-issued this guidance effective September 18, 2026. The reissued guidance replaces the previously issued Joint Guidance and provides clarification in response to questions and feedback received from School Administrative Units (SAUs), providers, and other interested parties. 

All IEP documents must reflect the updated guidance as soon as possible, but no later than thirty (30) days of the issuance of the guidance. 

Providers with current prior authorizations for School Health-Related Services through Acentra should upload any updated documentation to Atrezzo. Acentra will accept IEP language from both versions through October 18, 2026. Beginning October 19, 2026, Acentra will only accept IEP language from the new version re-issued on September 18, 2026. 

For technical assistance regarding the billing and processing of MaineCare claims, please contact your Provider Relations Specialist. 

For all other questions related to the provision of MaineCare School Health-Related Services, please contact Trista Collins, State Medicaid Educational Liaison.    

For technical information related to IEP development, please contact Dan Hemdal at the Maine Department of Education.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Contact: Danna Hayes

Danna.hayes@maine.gov

If You Bought Certain Generic Prescription Drugs in the United States Between May 2009 and December 2019, You Could be Eligible for Money

AUGUSTA – Attorney General Aaron M. Frey today joined a coalition of 45 states and territories seeking court approval of three settlements with Ascend Laboratories, Citron Pharma and Mayne Pharma to resolve allegations that the generic drug manufacturers engaged in a widespread, long-running conspiracy to artificially inflate and manipulate prices, reduce competition, and unreasonably restrain trade with regard to numerous generic prescription drugs.

Ascend will pay $400,000 to the states. Mayne will pay $650,000. Citron’s settlement only includes non-monetary terms as it has ceased business operations. As part of the settlement, the companies each agreed to meaningful injunctive terms including a series of internal reforms to ensure fair competition and compliance with antitrust laws. 

These latest settlements come as the States prepare for the first trial to be held in Hartford, Connecticut in February 2027.  

The States previously reached settlements with Sandoz, Glenmark, Lannett, Bausch, Apotex, Heritage, and Heritage’s parent company, Emcure, totaling $496.5 million.

If you purchased a generic prescription drug between May 2009 and December 2019, you may be eligible for compensation. To determine your eligibility, call 1-866-290-0182 (Toll-Free), email info@AGGenericDrugs.com or visit www.AGGenericDrugs.com. You can submit a claim for compensation.

Connecticut is leading a coalition of nearly all states and territories engaged in a series of antitrust cases, starting first in 2016. The first Complaint included Heritage and 17 other corporate Defendants, two individual Defendants, and 15 generic drugs. Two former executives from Heritage Pharmaceuticals, Jeffery Glazer and Jason Malek, have since entered into settlement agreements and are cooperating. The second Complaint was filed in 2019 against Teva Pharmaceuticals and 21 of the nation’s largest generic drug manufacturers. The Complaint names 16 individual senior executive Defendants. The third complaint, to be tried first, focuses on 80 topical generic drugs that account for billions of dollars of sales in the United States and names 26 corporate defendants and 10 individual defendants. The States filed a fourth complaint earlier this year, alleging that Novartis AG, Sandoz Group AG and Sandoz AG, are liable for Sandoz’s alleged conduct and for fraudulently transferring assets.

The cases all stem from a series of investigations built on evidence from several cooperating witnesses at the core of the different conspiracies, a massive document database of more than 20 million documents, and a phone records database containing millions of call detail records and contact information for more than 600 sales and pricing individuals in the generics industry. Each complaint addresses a different set of drugs and defendants and lays out an interconnected web of competing industry executives that met with each other during industry dinners, "girls’ nights out," lunches, cocktail parties, golf outings, and communicated via frequent telephone calls, emails, and text messages that sowed the seeds for their illegal agreements. Throughout the complaints, defendants use terms like "fair share," "playing nice in the sandbox," and "responsible competitor" to describe how they unlawfully discouraged competition, raised prices, and enforced an ingrained culture of collusion. Among the records obtained by the States is a two-volume notebook containing the contemporaneous notes of one of the States’ cooperators that memorialized his discussions during phone calls with competitors and internal company meetings over a period of several years.

States and territories also joining the settlements include: Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, the District of Columbia, Florida, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Puerto Rico, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, West Virginia, Wisconsin, and Wyoming.

MaineCare Coverage of Gender-Affirming Care for Medicaid Beneficiaries Under Age 18 and Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) Enrollees Under Age 19

Oct 09, 2026

As described in the message sent September 18, 2026, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) published a final rule in the Federal Register on August 13, 2026, that limits federal Medicaid and CHIP funding for certain gender-affirming care provided to minors. This rule prohibits federal matching funds for puberty blockers, cross-sex hormone therapy, and surgical interventions when used for gender transition for Medicaid beneficiaries under age 18 and CHIP enrollees under age 19. The federal rule is scheduled to take effect on October 13, 2026. 

The federal rule does not prohibit states from using state-only funds to cover these services. Maine law requires MaineCare to cover medically necessary treatment for or related to gender dysphoria and protects members from discrimination based on gender identity or gender expression.   

To ensure we are in compliance with this new federal rule, we have established the billing requirements below for providers who deliver gender-affirming care services to Medicaid beneficiaries under age 18 and CHIP enrollees under age 19. 

Effective on October 13, 2026, medical claims submitted through the MIHMS system must: 

  • Include applicable gender-affirming care diagnosis codes on all claims. 
  • Include the SE modifier on any claims submitted for gender-affirming care, other than behavioral health services.  
    • The SE modifier is used to identify a service that must be reimbursed using state-only funds.  
    • The SE modifier should be listed after any other modifiers on the applicable claim line(s). 
    • Behavioral health treatment for gender dysphoria is still eligible for federal match, so providers are not required to include the SE modifier on behavioral health-related claims.  

Effective on October 9, 2026, pharmacy claims submitted through the MEPOPS system must:  

  • Have Prior Authorization (PA) as required on the Department’s Preferred Drug List. This requirement applies to preferred and non-preferred products on the Department’s identified medication list.   
  • Include the medication’s intended clinical use by including the applicable diagnosis code and the information needed to determine the appropriate coverage and funding pathway.  
    • Medication prescribed for a clinical use outside the scope of 42 CFR § 441.801–441.802 and 457.476 remains subject to the otherwise applicable MaineCare pharmacy criteria. For medication prescribed for use within the scope of those provisions, the Department will review coverage under its separately funded state-only benefit.  

This PA requirement is used to determine clinical purpose and payment source. It does not, by itself, change the drug’s preferred status, establish additional step therapy, or mean that all uses of the medication are excluded from federally matched coverage. Existing drug-specific clinical criteria continue to apply as appropriate.  

For questions, please contact Provider Relations Specialist, Lisa Bouchard.

Maine eCourts Scheduled to be Implemented in Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc, and Waldo Courts in December

Date: 10/9/2026

The Maine Judicial Branch announced today that District and Superior Courts in Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc, and Waldo counties (comprising Judicial Region 6) will transition from paper filing to electronic filing (eFiling) on Monday, December 7, 2026. All case types in the Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc and Waldo County Unified Criminal Dockets (UCDs) and Superior Courts; and in the Belfast, Rockland, West Bath, and Wiscasset District Courts will transition to eFiling. To help attorneys and other stakeholders in Region 6 get ready for eFiling, the Judicial Branch will hold a virtual presentation by Zoom:

Topic: Maine eCourts in Region 6: Lincoln, Knox, Sagadahoc and Waldo County
Date & Time: Wednesday, October 14, 2026 at 12:00 p.m.
Please click the link below to join the webinar:
https://courts-maine-gov.zoom.us/j/96415858276
Passcode: 522889

The Zoom presentation will be recorded and posted on the Maine eCourts Training & Resources page following the live session.

eFiler Trainings for Attorneys and Staff
Members of the Maine eCourts project team will conduct in-person training for attorneys and staff according to the schedule below. Please note, registration is required to attend a training session. Prosecutors and staff will receive a separate link to register by email.

  • Prosecutor eFiler Training - Thursday, November 5th from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. (Knox County Superior Court, Rockland) Registration link to be sent by email
  • All Other eFiler Training Monday, November 2nd from 1:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. (Knox County Superior Court, Rockland) Register for this session

Region 6 Will Be the Second to Last Judicial Region to Complete the Transition to eFiling
When Region 6 courts transition to eFiling on December 7, they will be the second-to-last judicial region to implement eFiling. Earlier this year, courts in Judicial Regions 2, 7, 8, 1, and 4 made the switch from paper filing to eFiling. The Maine Judicial Branch remains on track to have all courts on the new system by February 2027.

Supreme Judicial Court Chief Justice Valerie Stanfill noted, "We are pleased that the transition from paper filing to eFiling has proceeded so smoothly this year, a testament to the hard work and dedication of all Judicial Branch staff. The eCourts project implementation and project support teams have traveled all over the state to make the transition successful, and they certainly deserve special acknowledgement."

Who Is Required to eFile?
Attorneys, government agencies (except law enforcement agencies), and parties who file more than six non-emergency cases in a calendar year, are required to eFile in courts that have implemented Maine eCourts. Self-represented parties are not required to eFile and can continue to file documents as they always have, in paper at the courthouse, by mail, or by email if filing a protection from abuse or harassment case.

About Maine eCourts
Maine eCourts is a suite of applications and web-based tools provided by Tyler Technologies' Enterprise Justice Software. The system allows for the management of court dockets and hearings, storage of digital case files, eFiling, and online payments.

For more information about Maine eCourts visit: https://www.courts.maine.gov/ecourts/index.html

To receive updates from the Maine Judicial Branch on Maine eCourts and other news, sign up for our mailing list at: https://www.courts.maine.gov/news/signup.html

item.content:encoded:
Hello, this is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

Well, it's getting more and more painful to fill up at a gas station or fill a tank of oil to heat your home. And we all know why.

Look, we're making progress shifting to other sources of energy to heat our homes, but we're still the most dependent on heating oil to heat our homes in the in the entire country. That reliance on heating oil makes us vulnerable to great shifts in global energy markets that drive up costs for Maine people and businesses. This president's war in Iran right now has created the largest fuel supply disruption in global history and has driven energy prices to record highs. The price of heating oil in Maine has reached more than $6 a gallon, so you'll be paying almost $800 more to fill a standard 275 gallon tank than you did a year ago. Kerosene prices are also reaching historic highs, all because of this war.

Maine people should not be forced to choose between staying warm or putting food on the table because the president chose to drag us into a needless war -- and an endless war, it appears.

My administration is doing what it can to help people save money on heating costs and stay comfortable in their homes this winter.

It's not enough, but I've directed the Department of Health and Human Services to identify households that would be eligible for $40 million in discounts on their electric bills through Maine's Low Income Assistance Program, or LIAP. Starting in November, thousands of eligible families who are customers of CMP or Versant will begin to see discounts ranging from 20 percent to 80 percent, and these will be applied automatically every month to their electric bills. It's one thing we can do. Families who already get federal assistance for home heating oil through LIHEAP, the Low Income Energy Assistance Program, will also be enrolled automatically in this state assistance program, LIAP, to get the maximum savings on their electric bills without any unnecessary paperwork. Customers with questions about this discount should contact their electric company directly.

I've also called on Congress to increase funding for federal home heating assistance, and I thank Maine's congressional delegation for their bipartisan support for LIHEAP funding, despite the president's attempts to eliminate this program. And that's just not enough, though, to make up for the skyrocketing costs driven by tariffs and the president's war. Congress must ensure the safety and comfort of Maine people heading into this winter season by increasing LIHEAP funding.

In the meantime, MaineHousing has distributed about $4 million to heating fuel companies for some of our most vulnerable households, those with older adults on small incomes or small children. Those trucks will begin delivering fuel to those homes over the next few days. We're also talking to farmers and foresters and other entities that use diesel fuel a lot about other ways we might be able to help them address high diesel prices here in Maine.

I'm proud to say that thanks to our investments over the years in energy efficiency and clean energy, our reliance on heating oil has fallen from 70 percent of Maine households in 2010 to just over 50 percent now. Still, it's not enough. My administration will continue to make it as affordable as possible to transition to clean energy sources like heat pumps, to save people money, and to make sure we're not left to shoulder the burden of the president's blunders.

Are you interested in exploring heat pumps or using wood or propane to heat your home instead of oil and kerosene? Are you curious about energy assistance programs? Weatherization? Do you need contact information for local community action agencies or MaineHousing or Efficiency Maine Trust? Our Winter Heating Guide, published every year by the Maine Department of Energy Resources, has all that information, as well as some helpful tips about winterizing and saving money, and about contact information, and links to online resources. You can view and download that Winter Heating Guide and review the latest heating fuel prices at Maine.gov/Energy.

This crisis affects all of us – low income, middle income, everyone who has a home, everyone who has a bill to pay this winter. But as the weather continues to get colder, I encourage all Maine people to see how they might save money and stay warm through the winter by using our current Maine Winter heating guide found at Maine.gov/Energy.

This is Governor Janet Mills. Please stay warm, and thank you for listening.

As an update to previous communications, we have launched the new MaineCare Partner Portal, which replaces the previous HealthPAS Online Portal. The MaineCare Partner Portal is now available for all regular functions, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.  

As a reminder, starting today, we are also changing how callers interact with and experience Provider Services and Member Services call center phone menus, known as Interactive Voice Response (IVR). Migrated Trading Partner Account Admin (R7) users

All other (delegated) users 

  1. Please contact your Admin (R7) user if you have not received an invitation to the MaineCare Partner Portal. You will receive an email link to register. This email will come from MEMMISDoNotReply@gainwelltechnologies.com. 
  2. Enter your invitation verification code, create a password, and set up an MFA method.

  • PDF RA – CARC 142 is not being reported for spenddown claims.   
  • 835 – CARC 96 and/or CARC 178 is being reported in error. 

As a workaround until the fix is in place, MaineCare will provide a report that can be accessed on the MaineCare Partner Portal. On the dashboard, navigate to Reports > Other Reports > “Spend Down Report.” This report will be available on Mondays for the claims finalized on the prior Wednesday. Because this week’s claims will be finalized on Thursday, the first report will be available no later than Tuesday, October 20, 2026.  

Hospital Crossover Claims 

Hospital crossover claims are not reporting the correct CARC when the member has Medicare and full MaineCare coverage, and the claim balance is for deductible or coinsurance.  In this situation, you would normally expect a B1 CARC. 

  • PDF RA – CARC B1 is being reported appropriately. 
  • 835 – CARC 45 is being reported in error. 

As a one-time workaround, MaineCare will provide a report after this issue has been resolved. On the dashboard, navigate to Reports > Other Reports > “Bad Debt Write off Report.” We anticipate this report will be available by November 13, 2026, and will confirm once the issue is resolved. 

Claims Processed in Excess of Charges 

Claims processed in excess of billed charges are not being reported with the appropriate CARC. 

  • PDF RA – Reporting CARC 94 appropriately. 
  • 835 – Claims that pay more than the billed amount (i.e. FQHC, Hospitals with APC, DRGs) are reporting CARC 45 instead of CARC 94. 

MaineCare does not have a workaround for this issue, as CARC 45 and CARC 94 share the same Claim Adjustment Group Code of CO (Contractual Obligation). MaineCare can provide a report upon request; please contact your Provider Relations Specialist.

The MaineCare TPL Exemption Request and Attestation Form is now available for TPL exemption request submission.  

Requesting TPL Exemption 

In accordance with MBM, Chapter I, Section 1.07 rules, MaineCare may assess the validity of extenuating circumstance or service code TPL exemption requests to bill MaineCare as the primary payer for services delivered to a member with primary, public, or commercial coverage. Providers wishing to apply for TPL exemption to bill MaineCare as the primary payer must complete and submit the MaineCare TPL Exemption Request and Attestation Form to the TPL Medicare Code Exempt Request email box.  

MaineCare will review completed forms with the supporting documentation and provide a decision letter of approval or non-approval via email to the requestor. An exemption request approval letter is valid only for a specific member for a defined duration, no greater than 12 months. The exemption request approval letter must be attached to all applicable MaineCare claims for dates of service during the approved time. Claims without a valid and up-to-date approval letter may result in denials.  

Providers are responsible for maintaining exemption request renewals by submitting a subsequent MaineCare TPL Exemption Request and Attestation Form at least 30 calendar days prior to the expiration date specified in the approval letter.

Oct 13, 2026

As previously communicated, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) requested all states develop and submit a comprehensive two-year provider revalidation strategy, with priority given to revalidating high-risk providers. 

You can find Maine’s two-year plan and a list of all providers included in the off-cycle revalidation on the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) Federally Required 2026-2028 Off-Cycle Revalidation Plan webpage. OMS grouped providers into five cohorts and sends notices alerting providers at least 30 days prior to initiating the revalidation window for their assigned cohort. OMS additionally sends a 60-day post-initiation notice, per standard revalidation practices.

Milestones to note:

Cohorts 1 & 2: Individual high-risk providers, providers without an NPI, Personal Care Agencies, Home Health Agencies, Hospice, and Assisted Living Services providers

You can find more information about the provider revalidation process on our Provider Enrollment and Revalidation webpage.

Questions?

For questions about this off-cycle revalidation process, please email Kenneth Jamison, Provider Enrollment Manager. item.description: MONROE, NY – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited six construction employers for willful and serious safety violations involving excavation hazards at the site of a planned 408,000 square-foot mixed-use commercial building and proposed a combined $648,094 in penalties. The department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration responded to an allegation of struck-by and collapse hazards associated with a large excavation at the Monroe Commons project – also known as Magna Square development – a planned 4-story, approximately 408,000 square-foot mixed-use commercial building with retail, office space, and a 39-room hotel located on an 18-acre site. The excavation had a steep, unstable embankment nearly 75 feet high which was not adequately sloped or shored. OSHA issued a total of 23 serious and five willful citations to the project’s general contractor and five subcontractors for failing to protect employees from cave-in, struck-by, and chemical hazards; neglecting to shield employees from falling or rolling rock and soil from an excavation face; and not ensuring daily inspections of excavations were conducted by a competent person. Advanced Plan and Build LLC, and subcontractors Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc. – operating as Drip Drop Waterproofing Inc. – and The Paving Masters LLC received citations for willfully exposing employees to cave-in and struck-by hazards from an unprotected excavation. OSHA also cited Advanced Plan and Build and The Paving Masters for their willful failure to ensure that the excavation, which was between 21 and 75 feet deep, was designed by a registered professional engineer. Subcontractors Century Max Industries Corp., DelValle Contractor, and Prime Structure Inc. were cited for serious violations for failing to protect employees from cave-in and struck-by hazards. DelValle and Parkstone Inc. and Obstacle Systems Inc. also received citations for serious violations related to lack of fall protection and chemical hazards.OSH

STATE OF MAINE SUPREME JUDICIAL COURT AMENDMENT TO MAINE RULES OF EVIDENCE
2026 Me. Rules 04
Effective: November 1, 2026
All of the Justices concurring therein, the following amendment to the Maine Rules of Evidence is adopted to be effective on the date indicated above. The specific amendment is stated below. To aid in the understanding of the amendment, an Advisory Note appears after the text of the amendment. The Advisory Note states the reason for recommending the amendment, but the Advisory Note is not part of the amendment adopted by the Court.
1. Rule 902 of the Maine Rules of Evidence is amended to read as follows:
RULE 902. EVIDENCE THAT IS SELF-AUTHENTICATING
The following items of evidence are self -authenticating; they require no extrinsic evidence of authenticity in order to be admitted:
. . . .
(13) Certified Records Generated by an Electronic Process or System. A record generated by an electronic process or system that produces an accurate result, as shown by a certification of a qualified person that complies with the certification requirements of Rule 902(11) or (12). The proponent must also meet the notice requirements of Rule 902(11).
(14) Certified Data Copied from an Electronic Device, Storage Medium, or File. Data copied from an electronic device, storage medium, or file, if authenticated by a process of digital identification, as shown by a certification of a qualified person that complies with the certification requirements of Rule 902(11) or (12). The proponent also must meet the notice requirements of Rule 902(11).
2 Advisory Note – November 2026
Subdivision (13) has been added to provide a procedure by which parties can authenticate certain electronic evidence other than through the testimony of a foundation witness. Title IV PostsecondaryInstitutions: Workforce Pell Program Applications Open for Second Review Cycle Through Nov. 13

October 14, 2026

For Immediate Release

Media Contact: Autumn Mahoney, Communications Specialist | media.dol@maine.gov

AUGUSTA -The State Workforce Development Board(SWDB) is accepting applications from Title IV postsecondary institutionsseeking stateapproval to offer programs eligible for federal Workforce Pell Grants. Applications for the second review cycle are due Friday, Nov. 13

Maine's Workforce Pell application provides an online process for eligible postsecondary institutions to seek approval to offer short-term workforce training programs that meet federal Workforce Pell Grant requirements. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed quarterly by the SWDB.

Workforce Pell expands federal Pell Grant eligibility to approved short-term workforce training programs that prepare students for high-skill, high-wage and in-demand careers. States are responsible for reviewing and certifying eligible programs before they are submitted to the U.S. Department of Education for final approval.

"Workforce Pell opens the door to new education and career opportunities for more people across our state,"said Vaughan Woodruff, chair of the State Workforce Development Board."The program's support for training that connects people with skills needed for Maine's workforce presents a significant opportunity for Maine workers and employers."

The Maine Workforce Pell Program Determination Policy establishesthe state's process foridentifying, reviewing and recommending eligible short-term workforce training programs for Workforce Pell. The policy was developed in partnership with the Maine Department of Labor, Maine Department of Education, Finance Authority of Maine, Maine Community College System and University of MaineSystem.

"Workforce Pell brings a new source of federal funding to Maine's short-term workforce training programs," said Maine Department of Labor Commissioner Laura Fortman. "We are excited to help Maine's postsecondary institutions take advantage of this opportunity to strengthen their programs, reach more students and prepare Maine's workforce for the future."

The SWDB will evaluate applications and make recommendations to the Governor for state certification. Programs certified by the Governor will then be submitted to the U.S. Department of Education for final approval. Following federal approval, the SWDB will publish the list of Maine-certified Workforce Pell programs on the Maine Workforce Pell webpage within 30 days.

Institutions can find the Workforce Pell application, eligibility requirements, program guidance and additional information on the Maine Workforce Pell webpage.
